messages:
maya: Quick heads-up - our sample-app Docker compose uses REDWOOD_API_KEY while SDKs prefer RW_API_KEY. New hires set REDWOOD_API_KEY and hit 401s after org key rotation.
liam: Is compose overriding local envs?
sam: Exactly. Locals export RW_API_KEY, compose injects REDWOOD_API_KEY into container, so both end up set. Current SDK precedence is RW_API_KEY > REDWOOD_API_KEY > ~/.redwood/credentials which creates ambiguity.
anika: Can you paste the compose snippet?
maya: services:
  web:
    environment:
      - REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY}

maya: The container ends up using the stale REDWOOD_API_KEY.
liam: Do SDK retries hide the error?
sam: SDK retries twice then surfaces error, but a few integrations swallow errors and keep retrying, which looks like transient failures.
anika: Quick fixes: 1) update sample apps to use RW_API_KEY only, 2) add entrypoint startup check that warns if both vars are present, 3) SDK should emit one WARN if repeated 401s at startup.
maya: I like 1+2 as a quick win. Suggested entrypoint message: WARNING: Both REDWOOD_API_KEY and RW_API_KEY set - using RW_API_KEY. Remove REDWOOD_API_KEY from env to avoid stale tokens. Docs: https://redwood.example/docs/auth
liam: Longer term: expose SDK_CRED_PRIORITY env (e.g., "RW,REDWOOD,FILE") so infra teams can configure precedence.
devex-bot: Note: support tickets flagged similar 401s last week (tickets #4521, #4527).
sam: Also propose a small parity CLI: `rw auth inspect` that prints which credential source will be used. Example output: Source: env(RW_API_KEY) | Value: set (redacted) | Config file: ~/.redwood/credentials - not present
manika: Agree, good for onboarding. Keep output minimal and machine-readable for scripts.
maya: I'll open a micro-PR to change compose and add the entrypoint check. @liam can you file follow-up issues for SDK_CRED_PRIORITY and rw auth inspect across node/python/go SDKs?
liam: Will do and link to the PR.
maya: Thanks all — should cut down onboarding 401 noise.
